entries.test: Public evaluations showing whether large language models improved beyond their June 2022 capabilities would test the asserted remaining headroom.
entries.note: “I in no way doubt” expresses firm confidence.

entries.test: The BIG-bench paper's reported results would show whether scaling produced progress on some measures but not others.
entries.note: “Wall” labels the reported absence of progress on particular measures.
This recommends a research direction without specifying a distinct outcome against which necessity could be tested.

entries.test: Public architectural documentation and component evaluations of a demonstrated AGI would show whether large-scale symbolic knowledge is crucial to its capabilities.
entries.note: Marcus explicitly presents and endorses his own earlier prediction; no arrival date is specified.

entries.test: Public architectural documentation and component evaluations of a demonstrated AGI would show whether explicit cognitive models are crucial to its capabilities.
entries.note: The prediction concerns an architectural requirement whenever AGI arrives.

entries.test: Public architectural documentation and component evaluations of a demonstrated AGI would show whether operations over variables, including storing, retrieving and comparing values, are crucial to its capabilities.
entries.note: The listed operations preserve the prediction's explicit scope.

entries.test: Public architectural documentation and component evaluations of a demonstrated AGI would show whether an explicit type/token distinction is crucial to its capabilities.
entries.note: The claim requires an explicit distinction, not merely behavior consistent with one.
Marcus proposes an additional capability for the research agenda. This passage does not itself predict that the capability will be achieved or specify a future outcome.

entries.test: Public Comprehension Challenge results for systems using only CNNs, RNNs and Transformers without writable latent discrete memory would test the prediction, with a successful system refuting it.
entries.note: “I think … will fail” expresses a forecast rather than a mere possibility. The architecture defines the systems covered, and no deadline is given.
